key_insight: This paper shows that Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) can be made practical for RL training rollouts by addressing the drop in acceptance rates that normally limits speculative decoding speedups. In simple terms: it helps RL training run faster without losing too much rollout quality.
problem_solved: The paper tackles the rollout bottleneck in reinforcement learning for large language models, where generating trajectories is slow and becomes the main training-time cost. It also addresses the common issue that MTP acceptance rates degrade during RL, reducing the expected acceleration.
method: Introduces Bebop, a systematic study of MTP behavior during LLM post-training and RL.
Applies rejection sampling to stabilize or improve acceptance behavior during speculative rollout generation.
Evaluates how MTP design choices affect speedup and quality, aiming to keep rollout acceleration effective throughout RL training.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this could significantly reduce RL training time for large language models by speeding up rollouts, which are often the dominant bottleneck. Faster training means lower compute cost and quicker iteration on alignment and post-training methods.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing RL training with rollout bottleneck highlighted

paper_title: Breaking Entropy Bounds: Accelerating RL Training via MTP with Rejection Sampling
paper_authors: Yucheng Li, Huiqiang Jiang, Yang Xu, Jianxin Yang, Yi Zhang
